GeneFox for R

R access to GeneFox’s shared scientific runtime, with data frames, tidyverse-compatible tables and SummarizedExperiment adapters. The wrapper is MIT licensed; the GeneFox engine and native runtime remain proprietary and are obtained separately.

This is version 1.1.0 of the package. It requires the GeneFox 1.1.0 runtime (ABI 1, SDK contract 1), which is distributed with the GeneFox 1.1.0 CLI; the GeneFox documentation describes how to install it.

Install the release’s source package from GitHub:

remotes::install_url(
  "https://github.com/vindhyadatascience/genefox-r/releases/download/v1.1.0/genefox_1.1.0.tar.gz")

pak::pak("url::https://github.com/vindhyadatascience/genefox-r/releases/download/v1.1.0/genefox_1.1.0.tar.gz") works too. Without remotes or pak, install jsonlite and digest first, then install.packages("<that URL>", repos = NULL, type = "source").

Or build a local checkout with R CMD build . and install its source tarball with R CMD INSTALL. A C compiler and the dependencies in DESCRIPTION are needed; building the wrapper does not compile or download the GeneFox engine.

After verifying a matching native runtime bundle’s publisher signature:

library(genefox)
session <- gf_session(runtime = "/path/to/genefox-runtime", output = "/path/to/results")
result <- gf_list_operations(session)
gf_table(result)
gf_close(session)

gf_runtime(path) validates the bundle’s platform, architecture, ABI, contract and file inventory before loading code. Digests check integrity and do not authenticate a publisher. Native runtime bundles are a separate GeneFox release deliverable; none is included here.

Use gf_to_tibble() or gf_to_data_table() for common table frameworks, and gf_from_se() / gf_to_se() for supported SummarizedExperiment data. GeneFox owns statistical analysis and figure rendering; the R package preserves the results, provenance and figures.

See the GeneFox documentation, and report problems in issues. The export’s genefox-source.json records its source commit and runtime compatibility.

Generated functions cover the free tools of the matching GeneFox runtime release. Inspect names(gf_tools(session)) in an open session to see what that runtime offers; a generated function never grants access to anything the runtime does not list.

To check the standalone R checkout, install the dependencies listed in DESCRIPTION, including the suggested packages for full interoperability coverage, and select a verified matching runtime bundle:

export GENEFOX_SDK_TEST_RUNTIME=/absolute/path/to/genefox-runtime
R CMD build .
GENEFOX_R_VERSION="$(Rscript -e 'cat(read.dcf("DESCRIPTION")[1, "Version"])')"
R CMD check --no-manual "genefox_${GENEFOX_R_VERSION}.tar.gz"

Building the tarball applies the package’s .Rbuildignore exclusions. The package check runs the files under tests/. Keep the runtime variable set to include the actual native and CLI transport checks.

GeneFox Pro in 1.1.0

GeneFox Pro needs a linked GeneFox account, and the 1.1.0 runtime offers no account linking outside the GeneFox app. Pro tools and Pro-only arguments (such as figure customization) are therefore not part of this package.

Data sources and terms

GeneFox analyzes public data that it retrieves from its providers when you run an analysis: TCGA and other projects through the NCI Genomic Data Commons, GEO, GTEx, the UCSC Xena and Toil recompute, CCLE, Treehouse, Expression Atlas and cBioPortal. That data remains subject to each provider’s terms, data-use policies and citation requirements, which you are responsible for following. Results carry their source and provenance so you can cite them.

Research use only

GeneFox is for research use only. It is not a medical device and must not be used to diagnose, treat or make clinical decisions about any person.

Notices

See LICENSE and inst/NOTICE. The GeneFox application, the genefox command-line tool and the GeneFox runtime are proprietary software of Vindhya Data Science and are not covered by this package’s license. The GeneFox name and logo are not licensed, except that the unmodified logo may accompany the credit “made with GeneFox” in reports produced with GeneFox, as inst/NOTICE describes.

Use gf_result_schemas() to inspect the output contracts shipped with this package, without starting a GeneFox runtime. The named list contains the versioned survival, table, figure, provenance and error JSON Schema documents. JSON arrays remain lists, and each call returns independent documents. These describe shared result blocks; tool-specific scientific payloads are preserved. Use gf_tools(session) for runtime availability.

Named success contracts cover list_operations, list_signature_presets, tcga_projects, gtex_tissue_expression, reference_ccle_expression, reference_treehouse_expression, reference_expression_atlas and reference_expression_atlas_catalog. Use each document’s x-genefox-tool field to identify the tool. Scientific values, nulls, display strings and trust-labelled fields retain their wire types. The nine released cBioPortal tools also have named success contracts: provider values, exact source probability strings, unavailable assays and separate patient/sample treatment counts retain their types and meanings.

Clinical and discovery output contracts also cover gene_info, list_coverage, tcga_cases, tcga_case_detail, tcga_cohort_summary, geo_search, geo_dataset_details and geo_supplementary_layout. Clinical age/survival units, unrequested versus empty file lists, unknown GEO sample counts, cursor state and parser diagnostics retain their original types. The supplementary diagnostic payload preserves its existing shape without tool or caveats members; its schema association is recorded in the result index.

In tcga_cohort_summary, check data.age_at_index.n before interpreting its quartiles. When no ages were observed (n = 0), the existing summary returns zero quartiles and the histogram is refused. Those zeros do not represent measured ages.

The TCGA analysis tools also publish named output contracts: tcga_expression, tcga_case_expression, tcga_compare_cohorts, tcga_differential_expression, tcga_gene_isoforms, tcga_gene_signature, tcga_heatmap, tcga_pan_cancer_expression, tcga_pan_cancer_survival, tcga_sample_pca, tcga_survival, tcga_top_correlates and tcga_tumor_normal. These describe scientific counts and measurements separately from display strings, canonical survival blocks, correlation/BH families, paired-test availability and export files. Sample counts and patient counts retain their distinct units. Infinite confidence bounds retain the producer’s string tokens; an unavailable measurement remains null. Heatmap color extents are automatically computed output measurements, marked x-genefox-output-role: computed_extent in the schema. Their presence does not enable custom input controls. Isoform measurements retain their separate pipeline and scale rather than being treated as a decomposition of the gene view.

GEO output contracts also cover geo_collection_summary, geo_finder_plan, geo_gene_correlation, geo_heatmap, geo_sample_pca, geo_series_expression, geo_survival and geo_top_correlates. The series expression schema includes its heatmap-delegation result. Collection fields and sample-evidence modes retain unknown counts, retry state, snapshots and the scope of subject linkage; neither aggregate certifies unique patients across datasets. Finder suggestions remain unexecuted and carry no fabricated fetch provenance.

GEO identifiers, source filenames, CSV headers, labels and ranked features retain their explicit trust labels. Count-library summaries describe the source matrix separately from retained samples. Survival discovery remains distinct from a computed endpoint, and the shared survival block counts samples while retaining the caller’s explicit time-unit mapping. Heatmap color extents remain computed output measurements. Scientific numbers and unavailable values retain their types.

Every tool in this package’s released catalogue has a named success contract in its result schemas. account_status preserves granted capability names and helper disclosures. tcga_chat_schema and geo_chat_schema describe read-only snapshots with actual analysis input schemas; they do not advertise chat execution. imported_de_enrichment keeps full-precision decimal strings, explicit Inf boundaries and null sample sizes; no sample counts are inferred from the imported table. open_destination preserves route plans, restore decisions, structured delegated results and untrusted run errors. These are additive output sidecars: the input catalogue, session ABI and SDK contract version remain unchanged. Contract presence does not grant access to a tool; consult the selected session’s tool listing.
